analysis.title: US Equities: Daily Short Activity (Securities Lending, Prime Brokerage), 10/2/2026
key_insights: GS Prime Brokerage securities-lending desk daily short-flow report as of 10/02/2026. The headline ex-ETF Short Index moved Day/Day -0.4% and the ETF Short Activity Index was Day/Day flat. The text does not give index levels.

Sector one-day short flow (the chart list is unlabeled in the text): Real Estate is the largest net short addition at +1.9%, and Technology is the largest net cover at -2.0% to -1.4% on the chart scale. The sector labels and values are listed in the same order, so the mapping is inferred from that order.
Top shorted industries by percent change: Mortgage REITs 5.4%, Hotel & Resort REITs 4.9%, Health Care REITs 4.4%, Ground Transportation 3.4%, Residential REITs 3.2%.

Top covered industries by percent change: Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals -2.7%, Electronic Equipment/Instruments/Components -2.6%, Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers -2.4%, Software -2.4%, Electrical Equipment -1.9%.

Largest GC (general collateral) names shorted by market value of short change: TSLA +6.2% short on a -0.2% price move, FDXF +54.2%, MU +5.1% (price +3.0%), GOOGL +2.0% (price -1.7%), NKE +5.6%, WELL +6.7%, RKLB +13.6%, ON +5.8% (price +4.2%), ITW +7.1%, HD +11.7%.

Largest GC names covered: AAPL -3.6%, SNDK -20.4% (price +2.7%), GEV -5.0% (price +3.9%), COHR -14.1% (price +10.9%), PANW -7.6%, INTU -12.9% (price +2.6%), CRM -6.3% (price +3.1%), VRT -2.5%, XOM -4.6%, ACN -2.7% (price +15.8%).
Largest NonGC names shorted: CBRS +9.0% (price -4.6%), BHP +4.1%, PSKY +5.9% (price -9.6%), SWKS +2.6%, INFY +1.6% (price +5.5%), ASTS +1.2%, CHH +2.2%, QBTS +1.8%, OKLO +1.4%, BXMT +7.0%.
Largest NonGC names covered: IONQ -4.4%, NBIS -1.9%, QXO -4.3% (price +3.1%), GIL -4.7%, RACE -4.3%, FRVO -3.4% (price +6.4%), GRAB -3.2%, LOAR -4.5%, DEO -4.2%, ARXS -2.2%.

Technology covering is broad across software and hardware names, and several covers coincided with price gains (SNDK, COHR, INTU, CRM, GEV, ACN). That pattern is consistent with short covering alongside rising prices on the day, but the report draws no conclusion.
Real Estate short additions are concentrated in REITs: CPT +41.6%, ARE +33.5%, WELL +6.7%, VTR +3.8%, with prices roughly flat to slightly lower.

Custom baskets (1-day change in short): Expensive Software (GSCBSF8X) covered 1.9%, Energy (GSXUENRG) shorted 2.9%, Artificial Intelligence (GSTMTAIP) covered 1.7%, Capex Beneficiaries (GSXUCAPX) covered 1.9%, AI At Risk (GSTMTAIR) shorted 3.7%.

Energy sector detail: SU +16.9% short, MKC +6.9% (consumer staples) and BTU +7.1%, versus covers in PBA -8.7%, XOM -4.6%, SHEL -4.1%, EXE -4.9%. Financials: SPGI +9.4% and MRSH +12.8% shorted, CG -16.9% and FAF -13.9% covered. Industrials: CACI +23.1% and TRU +11.5% shorted, ENS -18.8% and IR -9.3% covered.
The report is a data table with no rating changes, price targets or directional recommendations. The disclaimers state it is not research and not a basis for trading.
crypto_views: Crypto-linked equities appear in the short-flow tables: COIN is covered -3.6% (price +1.5%), HOOD covered -7.4% (price -1.2%), MSTR shorted +1.8% (price +4.8%) and IREN shorted +2.9% (price -0.6%).
risk_factors: Data comes from a subset of GS prime brokerage client positions and is not a full view of market short interest.
Report states past performance is not indicative of future results and that external vendor data is not verified by GS.
vol_and_positioning: Ex-ETF Daily Short Flow Short Index Day/Day -0.4%, ETF Short Activity Index Day/Day flat as of 10/02/2026.
AI At Risk basket (GSTMTAIR) saw short additions of 3.7% while the Artificial Intelligence basket (GSTMTAIP) saw covers of 1.7%.
Largest single short additions by size: FDXF +54.2%, CPT +41.6%, ARE +33.5%, CACI +23.1%, SU +16.9%, LQDA +17.4%, LIVN +15.0%, BNS +15.3%.
Largest single covers by size: MGEE -24.3%, SNDK -20.4%, ENS -18.8%, CG -16.9%, COHR -14.1%, FAF -13.9%, MAT -13.0%, INTU -12.9%.
CTVA shows +8.8% short against a -83.8% price change in the same row, which looks like a data or corporate-action artifact rather than a real price move.
